grades.reason: Exercises from a general OS textbook about race conditions, mutexes and semaphores; nothing about xv6 disabling interrupts while holding spinlocks.
Table of contents of xv6 that lists a section 'Locks and interrupts', but gives no explanation of why interrupts are disabled.
Covers mycpu/myproc and disabling interrupts so the CPU id stays valid; this is not about disabling interrupts while holding spinlocks.

grades.quote: To avoid this situation, if a spinlock is used by an interrupt handler, a CPU must never hold that lock with interrupts enabled. Xv6 is more conservative: when a CPU acquires any lock, xv6 always disables interrupts on that CPU.
grades.reason: Directly explains that an interrupt handler could try to acquire a spinlock already held on the same CPU and deadlock, so xv6 disables interrupts when acquiring any lock. It also covers the push_off/pop_off ordering.
